problem_statement: The checksum/crc16_ccitt.h API must expose eight functions with these signatures: uint16_t crc16_ccitt_aug_calc(const unsigned char *buf, size_t len); uint16_t crc16_ccitt_aug_update(uint16_t crc, const unsigned char *buf, size_t len); uint16_t crc16_ccitt_false_calc(const unsigned char *buf, size_t len); uint16_t crc16_ccitt_false_update(uint16_t crc, const unsigned char *buf, size_t len); uint16_t crc16_ccitt_kermit_calc(const unsigned char *buf, size_t len); uint16_t crc16_ccitt_kermit_update(uint16_t crc, const unsigned char *buf, size_t len); uint16_t crc16_ccitt_mcrf4xx_calc(const unsigned char *buf, size_t len); uint16_t crc16_ccitt_mcrf4xx_update(uint16_t crc, const unsigned char *buf, size_t len). Each *_calc function computes the named CRC16-CCITT variant over the whole input buffer, and each *_update function continues a previously computed CRC value over additional input. Splitting a message between a *_calc call and a *_update call must yield the same result as computing the whole message in one *_calc call. The results must match the standard checksums for CRC16-CCITT-AUG, CRC16-CCITT-FALSE, CRC16-CCITT-KERMIT, and CRC16-MCRF4XX.

verification.reason: The problem statement provides all eight function names with exact signatures, the required behavior (calc computes over the whole buffer, update continues a previous CRC, splitting must yield the same result), and states that results must match the standard checksums for the four named CRC16-CCITT variants. A competent embedded developer implementing these well-known standard CRC variants would produce the exact values the hidden tests check. The 'names needed not in the statement' list is empty, confirming all test-referenced symbols are covered.
